chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Sa'd ibn Abdillah from al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq al-Nahdi from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Sinan from a man from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, the Majestic and Exalted, revealed to David (peace be upon him): 'Indeed, a servant from among My servants will come to Me with a good deed, and I will admit him into My Paradise.' He (David) asked: 'O Lord, and what is that good deed?' He (Allah) replied: '(It is he who) enters upon My believing servant with joy, even if it is with a single date.' So David (peace be upon him) said: 'O Lord, one who has recognized You is deserving that he does not cut off his hopes from You.'
ai.seo_question: What is the specific good deed that guarantees entry into Paradise according to the revelation to Prophet David?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the profound spiritual weight of 'introducing joy' (idkhal al-surur) to a believer, illustrating that even a simple gift like a date can serve as a gateway to Paradise. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on social intimacy and emotional care as acts of worship, concluding with Prophet David’s affirmation that true gnosis of God sustains unwavering hope in His mercy.
